display.purpose: Page-level H2 headings, one per screen. Monospace (Martian Mono) for a control-panel register.

body.purpose: All standard UI copy, descriptions, list rows. IBM Plex Sans.

label.purpose: Uppercase, wide-tracked kicker line above every section or card title.

shadows.name: sheen
shadows.purpose: Applied to every resting Card; a faint top-lit bevel, never a lifted drop shadow.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default button variant. Signal Green fill, Deep Green Ink text — the single primary action in a view.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 2.5rem; padding: 0 1rem; border-radius: 1rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #22c55e; color: #052e16; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #16a34a; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #22c55e; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Bordered, transparent-fill variant for secondary actions (Cancel, Delete confirmation trigger).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #e2e8f0; border: 1px solid #1e293b; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(15,23,42,0.7); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: No border or fill at rest; lowest-emphasis action (nav items, inline icon actions).
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #94a3b8; border: none; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #0f172a; color: #e2e8f0; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pill badge family. Shown here in the Signal Green 'accent' variant; success/warning/destructive swap the hue but keep the same tinted-opacity recipe.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 10px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; border: 1px solid transparent; } .ds-badge-accent { background: rgba(34,197,94,0.1); border-color: rgba(34,197,94,0.2); color: #22c55e; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base surface for nearly every grouped block of content. Flat, no drop shadow, faint inset top sheen.

components.css: .ds-card { background: rgba(15,23,42,0.9); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); border: 1px solid #1e293b; border-radius: 1rem; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.04); padding: 1.5rem; } .ds-eyebrow { font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.18em; color: #94a3b8; margin: 0 0 4px 0; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; color: #e2e8f0; margin: 0 0 8px 0; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #94a3b8; margin: 0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Single-line text field. Border shifts to Signal Green on focus; no glow ring.
components.css: .ds-input { display: flex; height: 2.5rem; width: 100%; border-radius: 1rem; border: 1px solid #1e293b; background: rgba(2,6,23,0.7); padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #e2e8f0; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #94a3b8; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: #22c55e; }

narrative.overview:
Chain Hub v2 reads as a quiet, technical console you'd trust to run unattended overnight: near-black navy surfaces, restrained slate-gray text, and exactly one signal color that only lights up when something needs your attention. Headings run in a monospace display face (Martian Mono) against IBM Plex Sans body copy — a deliberate "engineering tool," not "consumer app," register. Cards sit flat with only the faintest inset sheen at their top edge instead of drop shadows; real elevation is reserved for the two things that actually float above the console: dialogs and the mobile navigation drawer.

The system explicitly rejects the look of a typical AI product — no gradients-as-decoration, no violet/purple SaaS palette, no rounded-blob illustrations. It is closer to a well-made local dev tool than a marketing surface.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome navy/slate base; one accent color used sparingly
Monospace display type paired with humanist sans body type
Flat surfaces with an inset top-highlight instead of drop shadows
Elevation appears only on dialogs and overlays, never on resting cards
Uniform ~16px corner radius ties cards, buttons, inputs, and menus together

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Green appears only on the single primary action per view, the active navigation item, and focus rings. If more than one element on a screen is fighting for Signal Green, that's a bug in the composition, not a case for a second accent.

rules.name: The Tinted-Opacity Badge Rule
rules.body: Every non-neutral badge (success/warning/destructive) uses the same recipe: border-{hue}-500/20, bg-{hue}-500/10, text-{hue}-300. Never a solid-fill badge.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every card or section that names a concept leads with an uppercase, wide-tracked label line before its title — never a title alone.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page surface itself casts a shadow. Depth is reserved for things that are genuinely above the page — dialogs, the mobile nav sheet — never for cards, buttons, or list rows sitting in the normal document flow.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Cards and interactive controls (buttons, inputs, menu items) share the same 1rem corner radius. A new component introducing a different large-surface radius breaks the console's visual unity.

dos: Do use only the semantic Tailwind tokens already in @theme (bg-background, text-foreground, border-border, bg-primary, etc.) — never a raw hex code or an arbitrary color value in a component.
Do keep Signal Green rare: one primary action, one active nav state, one focus ring per view.
Do give resting cards the inset sheen, never a drop shadow.
Do use lucide-react exclusively for icons, and sonner exclusively for toast feedback.
Do step card/grid padding and column count up from mobile (p-4/1-col) to desktop (sm:p-6/md:+xl: multi-col) rather than shrinking a fixed desktop layout.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color; status colors stay in their tinted-opacity badge lane, not as button or card fills.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, list rows, or anything resting in normal document flow.
Don't use arbitrary pixel values for spacing or radius; the system already resolves to one shared 1rem corner radius and Tailwind's default spacing scale.
Don't build a custom button/input/badge from scratch — extend the existing shadcn/ui primitives in components/ui/.
